abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

achor.title: Achor
achor.note: A valley near Jericho, on the border between Judah and Benjamin, named for the trouble Achan brought on Israel.

adrammelech.title: Adrammelech
adrammelech.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
adrammelech.note: A son of Sennacherib who killed his own father. The same name belongs to an Assyrian god the people of Sepharim sacrificed their children to after they were resettled in Samaria.

ahaz.title: Ahaz
ahaz.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahaz.note: He abandoned his predecessors' reforms, sacrificed his own son in the fire and closed the temple. Facing a coalition of enemies, he paid Assyria for protection instead of trusting the promise Isaiah brought, and Judah stayed an Assyrian vassal for a generation. The Immanuel prophecy was given in his crisis.

almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amoz.title: Amoz
amoz.about: Isaiah's father living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amoz.note: Isaiah's father, and not the prophet Amos: the names look alike in English but come from different Hebrew names entirely.

anathoth.title: Anathoth
anathoth.note: A priestly town in Benjamin, about three miles north of Jerusalem, and Jeremiah's home. He bought a field there as a sign of hope while announcing Jerusalem's fall. The site is identified with the village of Anata.

ar.title: Ar
ar.note: The chief city of Moab on the Arnon, so central that "Ar of Moab" could stand for Moab itself. God told Israel to leave it alone on the way through. Its ruins survive at Rabba in modern Jordan.

arabia.title: Arabia
arabia.note: Paul says he went away into Arabia for a time after his conversion, and in the New Testament the word covers the region south and east of Judea.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

ararat.title: Ararat
ararat.note: Noah's ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat as the floodwaters went down. The region is in what is now eastern Turkey.

ariel.title: Ariel
ariel.note: Isaiah's poetic name for Jerusalem, probably lion of God or altar hearth, in a prophecy of the city under siege and judged. A man called Ariel also turns up in Ezra 8:16.

arnon.title: Arnon
arnon.note: A swift river running into the Dead Sea from the east, the line between Amorite and later Moabite land and Israel's tribes beyond the Jordan. Its gorge still carries water in the Wadi al-Mujib. King Mesha of Moab's inscription, the Moabite Stone, boasts of building a highway across it.

aroer-2.title: Aroer
aroer-2.note: A second town of the name, in Numbers 32:34 and Joshua 13:25, on the same border between Israel's lands east of the Jordan and Ammonite territory.

arpad.title: Arpad
arpad.note: A Syrian city near Hamath. Assyrian kings kept naming it to show what they could conquer, and it fell to Tiglath-pileser III after a long siege around 740 BC. Its ruins are at Tell Rifaat, north of Aleppo.

asaph-2.title: Asaph
asaph-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asaph-2.note: Not David's singer. This Asaph is the one in 2 Kings 18:18 and Isaiah 36:3, and nothing else about him is recorded here.

ashdod.title: Ashdod
ashdod.note: Ashdod spelled another way, one of the five chief Philistine cities, on the coast between Ekron and Gaza. The captured ark was put in its temple of Dagon, and the affliction started there.

asshur.title: Asshur
asshur.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
asshur.note: Shem's son, whose name stuck to the land and empire of Assyria on the upper Tigris. Assyria became the great power of the eighth and seventh centuries BC, deported Israel's northern tribes after Samaria fell, and kept threatening Judah.

ava.title: Ava
ava.note: Also Ivah, a city in Mesopotamia from which the Assyrians sent settlers to fill Samaria after 722 BC. Sennacherib's field commander later named Ava's conquered gods, with those of Hamath and Sepharvaim, to push Hezekiah into surrender.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

baladan.title: Baladan
baladan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
baladan.note: His son was the Babylonian king who sent envoys to Hezekiah after his illness. About Baladan himself nothing else is recorded.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

beer-elim.title: Beer-elim
beer-elim.note: Isaiah's oracle against Moab names this well of the mighty ones as a border point the news of Moab's fall reached.

bel.title: Bel
bel.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
bel.note: Babylon's title for the god Marduk, which Isaiah and Jeremiah both mock as a powerless idol that will go into captivity itself when Babylon falls.

bozrah.title: Bozrah
bozrah.note: Edom's capital, the city of the early Edomite king Jobab. The prophets kept coming back to it in their oracles against Edom. Isaiah pictures the Lord coming from Bozrah in stained garments.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

carchemish.title: Carchemish
carchemish.note: A major city on the west bank of the Euphrates. For a long time it was a Hittite provincial capital, and later the seat of a Neo-Hittite kingdom of its own. Nebuchadnezzar crushed Pharaoh Necho's army there.

carmel.title: Carmel
carmel.note: Elijah's contest with the prophets of Baal happened on this mountain ridge on Israel's Mediterranean coast. Fire came down from heaven when Elijah prayed, and Baal had nothing to answer with.

chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

chush.title: Chush
chush.note: Cush as a land. It lay south of Egypt, roughly modern Sudan and Ethiopia, and the Old Testament keeps coming back to it as a distant, exotic country.

cyrus.title: Cyrus
cyrus.about: Emperor living at the time of Exile and Return
cyrus.note: The Persian king who took Babylon and let the deported peoples, the Jews among them, go home and rebuild their temples. Isaiah calls him by name long before he was born, God's shepherd and anointed. The Cyrus Cylinder, found in Babylon in 1879, records the same policy.

damascus.title: Damascus
damascus.note: A city has stood here, on a fertile plain watered by the Barada northwest of Mount Hermon, since before the patriarchs. It was the Aramean capital that fought Israel through the ninth and eighth centuries BC. Saul was converted on the road into it, and the street called Straight was a real colonnaded street whose columns have been found.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

dedanim.title: Dedanim
dedanim.note: Isaiah pictures their caravans camping in the desert thickets, and Ezekiel has them supplying Tyre. They are generally placed at the oasis of al-Ula in northwest Arabia, where Dedanite and Lihyanite inscriptions confirm a real trading kingdom.

dibon.title: Dibon
dibon.note: A Moabite city Israel took and rebuilt. King Mesha names it on the Moabite Stone as one of his own building projects.

dimon.title: Dimon
dimon.note: Isaiah sees the waters of Dimon, east of the Dead Sea, turning to blood in his oracle against Moab. Many take it as another name for the waters of Dibon, the Moabite capital where Mesha's stone was found.

dumah-2.title: Dumah
dumah-2.note: Named once, in Isaiah, and nowhere else.

eden.title: Eden
eden.note: The garden where God put the first humans. A river ran out of it and split into four, the Tigris and the Euphrates among them, which is why most people look for it in the lowlands of ancient Mesopotamia. Its exact site cannot be fixed.

eden-2.title: Eden
eden-2.note: A region in northern Mesopotamia, not the garden. It sold richly worked cloth to Tyre, and the Rabshakeh named it outside Jerusalem among lands Assyria had already taken. Many identify it with Bit-Adini on the middle Euphrates, which Shalmaneser III annexed.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

eglaim.title: Eglaim
eglaim.note: Isaiah's oracle says Moab's wailing carries as far as Eglaim. It is probably the En-eglaim of Ezekiel 47:10.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

elam.title: Elam
elam.note: A kingdom east of Babylon. In the prophets it is one of the nations among which God scattered Israel. Its people turn up again at Pentecost.

elealeh.title: Elealeh
elealeh.note: Reuben rebuilt this town on the grazing plateau east of the Jordan for its herds. By Isaiah's and Jeremiah's time Moab had it back, and both name it in their oracles. The ruin el-Al, just northeast of Heshbon, is the site.

eliakim.title: Eliakim
eliakim.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
eliakim.note: Hezekiah's palace administrator, sent with the other officials to talk to the Rabshakeh while Sennacherib had Jerusalem under siege. Another Eliakim was the king Necho renamed Jehoiakim.

ephah-4.title: Ephah
ephah-4.note: Named once, in Isaiah, and nowhere else.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

esar-haddon.title: Esar-haddon
esar-haddon.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
esar-haddon.note: Sennacherib was murdered and Esarhaddon took the Assyrian throne after him. He carried Manasseh of Judah off to Babylon, and his own inscriptions list Manasseh among the vassal kings paying him tribute.

gaba.title: Gaba
gaba.note: Another English spelling of Geba, a Levitical city in Benjamin by the pass of Michmash. Jonathan raided a Philistine garrison there, and later it marked the line between the northern and southern kingdoms.

galilee.title: Galilee
galilee.note: Jesus grew up here and did most of his public work around the Sea of Galilee. Judeans thought the north provincial and mixed, which is the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come out of Nazareth.

gallim.title: Gallim
gallim.note: Michal was given to Palti of Gallim after Saul took her away from David. Isaiah lists the town, in Benjamin north of Jerusalem, among the places panicking as the Assyrian army comes on.

gebim.title: Gebim
gebim.note: A village just north of Jerusalem, and the name probably means cisterns. Isaiah pictures its people running as an invading army closes on the city.

gibeon.title: Gibeon
gibeon.note: They tricked Joshua into a treaty by dressing as travellers from far away, the Hivites of this city northwest of Jerusalem, and so they lived but served at Israel's sanctuary. The tabernacle stood at Gibeon for years, and Solomon had his dream there. At el-Jib dozens of jar handles stamped with the name have settled where it was.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

gomorrah.title: Gomorrah
gomorrah.note: Destroyed with Sodom for its wickedness, and the two became shorthand for a people ripe for judgment, from Moses through Jesus and the apostles. No remains have been confirmed. It is generally placed near the southern basin of the Dead Sea.

gozan.title: Gozan
gozan.note: When Assyria took the northern kingdom, it resettled Israelite captives in this region of northern Mesopotamia.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hanes.title: Hanes
hanes.note: An Egyptian city in Isaiah's warning to the envoys Judah sent looking for an alliance with Egypt. It is generally identified with Herakleopolis Magna, near Ihnasiya el-Medina, south of Cairo.

haran.title: Haran
haran.note: Abraham's family stopped and settled here for a while on the way toward Canaan, and Abraham set out again from Haran in Genesis 12:4. The city was likely named after his brother.

hena.title: Hena
hena.note: The Assyrian messenger names it to Hezekiah as one more city Assyria has already taken. It is usually identified with Anah on the Euphrates, near Sepharvaim.

hephzi-bah.title: Hephzi-bah
hephzi-bah.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hephzi-bah.note: My delight is in her. She was Hezekiah's wife and Manasseh's mother. Isaiah takes the same name for Jerusalem restored, no longer the abandoned wife.

heshbon.title: Heshbon
heshbon.note: Sihon's capital, east of the Jordan near the northern edge of Moab. Moses took it before Israel crossed into Canaan, and it became a Levitical city in Reuben. Moab later had it back, which is why the prophets name it in their judgments on Moab, and the ruins, still called Hesban, lie about twenty miles east of the Jordan.

hezekiah.title: Hezekiah
hezekiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hezekiah.note: One of Judah's few good kings. He came after Ahaz, reopened the temple, tore down the high places, and broke up the bronze serpent Moses had made once people began worshipping it. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem in 701 BC, Hezekiah prayed, Isaiah promised deliverance, and the siege broke overnight. His seal impression has been dug up near the Temple Mount, and his tunnel still runs under the city.

hillkiah-2.title: Hillkiah
hillkiah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hillkiah-2.note: Known through his son, the palace official who went out to meet the enemy's envoys at the wall, in 2 Kings 18 and again in Isaiah 36. Nothing else is recorded about him.

horonaim.title: Horonaim
horonaim.note: A Moabite town south of the Arnon, and Isaiah and Jeremiah both name it among the towns that would fall. The name means "two hollows". Where it was is not known for sure.

immanuel.title: Immanuel
immanuel.about: Man living at the time of the New Testament
immanuel.note: "God with us." Isaiah gave the name to King Ahaz as a sign that the danger to Judah would pass before a child called by it was old enough to know right from wrong. Matthew applies it to Jesus' birth, and which child Isaiah first had in view is still argued over.

isaiah.title: Isaiah
isaiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
isaiah.note: Amoz's son, a prophet in Jerusalem in the eighth century, who counselled four kings of Judah and is quoted in the New Testament more than any other prophet. He gave his two sons names that were sermons, Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem he told Hezekiah the city would stand, and the Taylor Prism brags of the siege without ever claiming the city fell.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jaazer.title: Jaazer
jaazer.note: Jazer, an Amorite town in Gilead east of the Jordan. Israel took it and gave it to Gad, then to the Levites of Merari. Isaiah and Jeremiah both use its ruined vineyards as a picture of Moab's ruin.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jah.title: Jah
jah.note: A short, poetic form of Yahweh, God's covenant name. It turns up mostly in the Psalms, and it is the end of Hallelujah, "praise Yah".

jahaz.title: Jahaz
jahaz.note: Moses beat Sihon, the Amorite king, at Jahaz, on the plateau north of the Arnon. The town went to Reuben and then to the Merarite Levites, and because it changed hands with Moab more than once, Isaiah and Jeremiah both name it in their oracles against Moab.

javan.title: Javan
javan.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
javan.note: Japheth's fourth son in the table of nations. The Hebrews took his descendants to be the Ionians, the Greek world, and the prophets use Javan to mean Greece and its merchants. Modern Hebrew still calls Greece by the name.

jeberechiah.title: Jeberechiah
jeberechiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeberechiah.note: When Isaiah wrote on a tablet in the days of Ahaz, he took Jeberechiah's son Zechariah as a witness.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jeshurun.title: Jeshurun
jeshurun.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jeshurun.note: It is a pet name for Israel, "the upright one", used a few times in Deuteronomy and Isaiah, and usually it comes right before the text shows how far from upright Israel was.

jesse.title: Jesse
jesse.about: David's father living at the time of United Monarchy
jesse.note: Obed's son and Boaz and Ruth's grandson, a man of some standing in Bethlehem with eight sons, the youngest David. Isaiah's "stem of Jesse" is David's family, and the "root of Jesse" is the Messiah. The last we see of him, David is getting him a safe place with the king of Moab.

jetheth.title: Jetheth
jetheth.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
jetheth.note: Edom had clan chiefs who came down from Esau, and Jetheth is listed with them.

joah.title: Joah
joah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
joah.note: The royal recorder, sent out with the other officials to talk to the Rabshakeh when Sennacherib's army sat outside Jerusalem.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

jotham.title: Jotham
jotham.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jotham.note: He carried on his father Uzziah's steady rule in Judah, building up Jerusalem's defences and bringing the Ammonites under, and Scripture counts him one of the few kings who did right in the Lord's eyes. The high places stayed, though.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kedar.title: Kedar
kedar.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
kedar.note: Ishmael's son, and the father of a desert tribe known for dark tents and good archers. Poets use Kedar for far-off wilderness living, and the Song of Solomon uses it for dark beauty.

kir.title: Kir
kir.note: Amos says God brought the Arameans from Kir the way he brought Israel out of Egypt, and he warns that Damascus will be sent back there. Tiglath-pileser III did exactly that in 732 BC, and his own annals record it. Isaiah's Kir, set beside Elam in a scene of soldiers arming, may or may not be the same place.

kir-2.title: Kir
kir-2.note: Named once, in Isaiah, and nowhere else.

kir-haraseth.title: Kir-haraseth
kir-haraseth.note: Moab's fortress capital, modern Kerak in Jordan. When Mesha of Moab rebelled after Ahab died, Israel, Judah and Edom besieged him there, and he sacrificed his own son on the wall, which ended the siege. His own account of the revolt survives on the Moabite Stone, found in 1868.

lachish.title: Lachish
lachish.note: A heavily fortified Canaanite royal city in Judah's lowlands. Joshua took it, Rehoboam rebuilt it into one of Judah's strongest fortresses, and in 701 BC Sennacherib's Assyrians took it again. Assyria carved the siege on wall reliefs now in the British Museum. The ruins at Tell ed-Duweir also gave up the Lachish Letters, written during Babylon's last siege, just before Jerusalem fell.

laish.title: Laish
laish.note: Peaceful, cut off, and Canaanite. The tribe of Dan, having failed to settle the land it was given, took the city and renamed it Dan.

lasharon.title: Lasharon
lasharon.note: "Belonging to Sharon." Joshua beat a king of Lasharon, but most of these verses are about the Sharon plain, the rich coast between Joppa and Mount Carmel, with royal pasture and some of Gad living there. Its beauty became a byword, "the rose of Sharon," and Isaiah pictures it blooming again.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

libnah.title: Libnah
libnah.note: A royal Canaanite city near Lachish that Joshua took and gave to the Levites in Judah. It held out against Sennacherib's Assyrians. Hamutal, Josiah's wife and mother of two of Judah's last kings, came from there.

lud.title: Lud
lud.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
lud.note: Shem's son. His people are usually taken to be the Lydians of Asia Minor. Some later passages may mean a people in Africa instead.

luhith.title: Luhith
luhith.note: In Isaiah and Jeremiah, refugees climb the road up to Luhith in Moab weeping. It was somewhere between Zoar and Horonaim, exactly where is unknown.

madai.title: Madai
madai.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
madai.note: Japheth's son, and the ancestor of the Medes, who later joined Persia in taking Babylon.

madmenah.title: Madmenah
madmenah.note: Its people run in Isaiah's picture of an army coming down on Jerusalem from the north, one village in a list with Anathoth and Nob.

maher-sha-lal-bash-baz.title: Maher-sha-lal-bash-baz
maher-sha-lal-bash-baz.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
maher-sha-lal-bash-baz.note: Isaiah's son, and the name was the message: "quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil." Before the boy could say father or mother, Assyria would strip Damascus and Samaria. Isaiah had the name written on a large tablet, with two reliable men as witnesses, before the child was born.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

mearah.title: Mearah
mearah.note: "The cave," near Sidon on the Phoenician coast, one of the places on the northern frontier still not taken in Joshua's day. A cave near Jezzine in the mountains east of Sidon has been suggested, but no one is sure.

medeba.title: Medeba
medeba.note: An old Moabite town given to Reuben. Joab beat the Ammonites and their Aramean allies near it in David's time, and Moab later took it back, which Isaiah mourns in his oracle against Moab. Today it is Madaba in Jordan, known for a sixth-century Byzantine floor mosaic that is the oldest surviving map of the Holy Land.

merodach-baladan.title: Merodach-baladan
merodach-baladan.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
merodach-baladan.note: A Chaldean chief who seized Babylon's throne and fought Assyria in the late eighth century BC. He sent envoys to Hezekiah when the king got well, probably looking for an ally, and Hezekiah showed them everything in his treasury, which brought Isaiah's warning of exile to Babylon. Assyrian records of Sargon II and Sennacherib know him as Marduk-apla-iddina II.

midian.title: Midian
midian.note: A people descended from Abraham through Keturah, and they keep turning up in different roles. Midianite traders bought Joseph. Moses found a home and a wife, Zipporah, in Midian. Later they oppressed Israel until Gideon beat them.

migron.title: Migron
migron.note: Saul camped under a pomegranate tree at Migron, near Gibeah, with about six hundred men, just before Jonathan's raid on the Philistines at Michmash. Isaiah has an invading army pass a Migron near Aiath, apparently a different spot of the same name.

mikmas.title: Mikmas
mikmas.note: Michmash, a town in Benjamin north of Jerusalem. The Philistines gathered there against Saul, and Jonathan and his armour-bearer climbed across a rocky ravine to attack their garrison, which set off a rout. Isaiah pictures the Assyrian army leaving its baggage there, and families from Michmash came back from Babylon.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nebaioth.title: Nebaioth
nebaioth.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
nebaioth.note: Ishmael's firstborn. His descendants were an Arabian trading people, named next to Kedar in Isaiah.

nebo.title: Nebo
nebo.note: The mountain in Moab where Moses looked over the promised land before he died, taken as Jebel Neba on the ridge of Pisgah east of the Dead Sea. A Reubenite town nearby had the same name, and the oracles against Moab condemn it.

nebo-3.title: Nebo
nebo-3.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
nebo-3.note: Isaiah names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

nimrim.title: Nimrim
nimrim.note: Isaiah and Jeremiah both name the waters of Nimrim, a once-fertile spot in Moab, in their oracles of judgment against that country.

nineveh.title: Nineveh
nineveh.note: The capital of the Assyrian empire. Jonah preached there against his will and watched the city repent, and Nahum later announced its destruction once it had gone back to its old cruelty.

nisroch.title: Nisroch
nisroch.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
nisroch.note: Sennacherib, king of Assyria, was killed by his own sons in the temple of Nisroch, an Assyrian god and not a man at all.

noah.title: Noah
noah.about: Flood survivor living at the time before the Flood
noah.note: God picked him as the one righteous man of his generation and told him to build an ark. His family came through the flood with him, along with pairs of every kind of animal. Afterward God made a covenant with him.

nob.title: Nob
nob.note: A town of priests near Jerusalem. David came here running from Saul, and the priest Ahimelech gave him the consecrated bread and Goliath's sword. Saul had the priests of Nob killed for it.

noph.title: Noph
noph.note: Memphis, under its Hebrew name, which several prophets use when they speak of Egypt's coming judgment.

ophir.title: Ophir
ophir.note: It was the gold that made Ophir famous across the ancient world. Solomon's ships, sailing with Hiram of Tyre, brought it back in quantity, and the place itself was likely in southern Arabia or along the Red Sea.

oreb.title: Oreb
oreb.note: He was one of two Midianite commanders the men of Ephraim killed during Gideon's rout, and the rock where he died took his name.

palestina.title: Palestina
palestina.note: The King James word for Philistia, the Philistines' strip of coast along the Mediterranean.

pathros.title: Pathros
pathros.note: Upper Egypt. Jewish refugees fled there, and the prophets name it among the places God promised to gather his scattered people back from.

pekah.title: Pekah
pekah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
pekah.note: He took the northern throne by murdering the king before him. Then he joined Syria against Assyria, invaded Judah, and tried to force King Ahaz into the alliance.

perazim.title: Perazim
perazim.note: The prophet Isaiah warns that the Lord will rise against his own people the way he once rose up at Mount Perazim. The earlier victory there is almost certainly David's battle with the Philistines.

pharaoh-5.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-5.note: In the divided-kingdom years this was the Egypt people were tempted to lean on, mocked as a broken reed that pierces the hand of whoever leans on it, and Isaiah warned against going down to Pharaoh for help.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

pul-2.title: Pul
pul-2.note: Named once, in Isaiah, and nowhere else.

rabshakeh.title: Rabshakeh
rabshakeh.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
rabshakeh.note: A title, not a name: a senior Assyrian officer. During Sennacherib's siege he stood outside Jerusalem's walls and taunted the people in Hebrew, trying to break them over the heads of their leaders.

rahab-2.title: Rahab
rahab-2.note: Not the woman from Jericho. This Rahab is the sea monster the poets use for chaos, and by extension a nickname thrown at Egypt.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

remaliah.title: Remaliah
remaliah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
remaliah.note: Pekah's father. Isaiah keeps calling Pekah "the son of Remaliah," and it is not meant kindly.

rezeph.title: Rezeph
rezeph.note: Sennacherib's field commander named it as proof that no god had saved anyone from Assyria. Usually identified with Rasappa.

rezin.title: Rezin
rezin.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
rezin.note: King of Aram-Damascus. He and Pekah of Israel came against Judah together, and Ahaz panicked and turned to Assyria instead of trusting Isaiah's word that the threat would pass.

sabean.title: Sabean
sabean.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
sabean.note: Traders from Sheba in southern Arabia. Isaiah 45:14 says their wealth will come over to Israel's God.

samaria.title: Samaria
samaria.note: Omri bought a hill from a man called Shemer and built a capital on it. Samaria took over from Tirzah as the seat of the northern kingdom. Ahab and the kings after him ruled from there.

sarah.title: Sarah
sarah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
sarah.note: Abraham's wife. She was ninety when Isaac was born, after decades of being unable to have children, and earlier she had doubted the promise could come through her at all.

sargon.title: Sargon
sargon.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
sargon.note: Sargon II took the Assyrian throne after Shalmaneser V died, around 722 BC. His annals from Khorsabad claim he conquered Samaria and carried off 27,290 of its people, though the Babylonian Chronicle gives the city to Shalmaneser and most historians read Sargon as taking his predecessor's credit.

saul.title: Saul
saul.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
saul.note: Israel's first king, found while he was out looking for his father's lost donkeys and anointed by Samuel in private before the tribes confirmed him.

seba-2.title: Seba
seba-2.note: He was a son of Cush, and his descendants are tied to a kingdom somewhere in Africa or Arabia. The Psalms have it bringing tribute.

seir.title: Seir
seir.note: A rough range of mountains east of the Arabah. It runs from the bottom of the Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqabah. The Horites lived there first, and Esau's descendants pushed them out.

sennacherib.title: Sennacherib
sennacherib.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
sennacherib.note: He besieged Jerusalem in Hezekiah's reign and boasted in his own inscriptions that he shut Hezekiah up like a bird in a cage. He never claims he took the city.

sepharvaim.title: Sepharvaim
sepharvaim.note: A city the Assyrians took. They moved its people into Samaria after deporting Israel, and they became part of the mix that later made up the Samaritans.

sharezer.title: Sharezer
sharezer.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
sharezer.note: He and his brother Adrammelech killed their own father, Sennacherib, king of Assyria. Both 2 Kings and Isaiah record it in a line.

shear-jashub.title: Shear-jashub
shear-jashub.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shear-jashub.note: Isaiah's son, whose name was a message, a remnant shall return, and Isaiah took the boy with him when he went out to meet King Ahaz.

sheba.title: Sheba
sheba.note: The Queen of Sheba came a long way, probably from southern Arabia. She came to test Solomon with hard questions. She went home saying the reports she had heard did not tell the half of it.

shebam.title: Shebam
shebam.note: Good grazing land east of the Jordan, taken from Sihon, which Reuben and Gad asked for because of their flocks.

shebna.title: Shebna
shebna.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shebna.note: He ran Hezekiah's palace. He was also carving himself a grand tomb, and Isaiah told him he would be thrown out of office and die in a foreign land. Eliakim would take his place.

shihor.title: Shihor
shihor.note: The stream on Egypt's northeastern border. It marks the southwestern edge of the land promised to Israel.

shiloah.title: Shiloah
shiloah.note: Isaiah set the quiet waters of Shiloah, a gentle channel bringing water from the Gihon spring into Jerusalem, against the flood of the Euphrates. The people had turned down the one, and the other was coming. It was later linked with the pool of Siloam.

shinar.title: Shinar
shinar.note: The old name for the land of Babylon. The tower of Babel went up there, and much later it was the heart of Nebuchadnezzar's empire.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

sinim.title: Sinim
sinim.note: Isaiah 49:12 names it once, as a far land God will gather his scattered people from, with the north and the west. Where it was has never been settled.

sodom.title: Sodom
sodom.note: Sodom was destroyed by fire from heaven along with Gomorrah, and the rest of Scripture keeps pointing back to it as the picture of judgment. It was one of the cities of the plain near the Dead Sea.

tabeal.title: Tabeal
tabeal.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
tabeal.note: Two men share the name. Isaiah 7:6 makes one the father of the man Syria and Israel meant to put on Judah's throne instead of Ahaz, and Ezra 4:7 has the other, an official in Samaria who wrote to Artaxerxes against the walls.

tarshish.title: Tarshish
tarshish.note: Far to the west, at the edge of what Israel knew of the sea. Solomon's ships went there for gold, and ships of Tarshish came to mean any big ocean-going ship. Jonah boarded one at Joppa to get away from Nineveh.

tartan.title: Tartan
tartan.note: An Assyrian title, roughly commander-in-chief, not a man's name. One tartan came with the delegation demanding Jerusalem's surrender from Hezekiah, and an earlier one took Ashdod for Sargon.

telassar.title: Telassar
telassar.note: The Assyrian king's messenger names it with Gozan and Haran, places already conquered. The children of Eden lived there, somewhere in Mesopotamia.

tema.title: Tema
tema.note: An oasis in the north Arabian desert, on the caravan road between Damascus and the Arabian interior, named for a son of Ishmael. Job's friend Eliphaz compares Job's useless helpers to the caravans of Tema. Much later the Babylonian king Nabonidus made it his residence.

tirhakah.title: Tirhakah
tirhakah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
tirhakah.note: The Kushite pharaoh of Egypt in the early seventh century BC, known in his own records as Taharqa. Word that he was marching against Assyria made Sennacherib send Hezekiah a threatening letter during the siege of Jerusalem.

tophet.title: Tophet
tophet.note: The place in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned to Molech, until Josiah defiled it. Jeremiah said the valley would fill with the dead. Later Jewish pictures of Gehenna drew on it.

tubal.title: Tubal
tubal.note: In the prophets Tubal is a far northern people, usually named with Meshech, trading and making war. The name goes back to a son of Japheth.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

uriah-2.title: Uriah
uriah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
uriah-2.note: A priest, not the Hittite. 2 Kings 16 has him at work in the temple, and Isaiah 8:2 calls him as a witness.

uzziah.title: Uzziah
uzziah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
uzziah.note: King of Judah at sixteen, he reigned fifty-two years and rebuilt the army and the economy. Then he went into the temple to burn incense himself, which no king was allowed to do. The priests confronted him and leprosy broke out on his forehead while he stood there.

zachariah-21.title: Zachariah
zachariah-21.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zachariah-21.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. Isaiah names him once.

zebulun.title: Zebulun
zebulun.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulun.note: Jacob's tenth son and Leah's last. His tribe's land ran up to the Sea of Galilee, and Isaiah names it with Naphtali as the place where a light would dawn, which Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.

zion.title: Zion
zion.note: The fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David took from the Jebusites and called the city of David. He built his palace there. Archaeologists have uncovered the Stepped Stone Structure on that ridge, and many tie it to David's time.

zoan.title: Zoan
zoan.note: Tanis, to the Greeks, a city in the Nile delta that was once Egypt's capital. Numbers says it was built seven years after Hebron. The psalmist puts the plagues in the field of Zoan.

zoar.title: Zoar
zoar.note: Lot asked that this little town be spared so he could run to it, and it was, while Sodom and Gomorrah burned. It was first called Bela, and it lay where Moab met the Dead Sea plain.
